name: Forbidden Palace
note: The imperial seat of the Ming and Qing dynasties. The field notes point foreign visitors to the separate Palace Museum booking website.

name: National Museum of China
note: Artifacts tracing Chinese civilization through its major dynasties. A pick for a big China history buff; the field notes recommend booking through the mini-app.

name: Tiananmen Square
note: A busy central stop, with the Chairman Mao Memorial Hall and the Monument to the People’s Heroes.

name: Qianmen
note: Touristy shopping, famous Peking duck spots Bianyifang and Quanjude, and hutongs to the east. The MUJI hotel caught my eye.

name: Temple of Heaven
note: A huge park and imperial ritual complex. The Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests is the highlight; also a place to watch people playing chess. Nearby: CABO Coffee. My verdict on Hongqiao Pearl Market: skip it.

name: Wangfujing
note: Shopping from luxury to anime and manga. Donglaishun for lamb hotpot with sesame paste is my dinner recommendation.

name: Ming City Wall Relics Park
note: A surviving section of the old city wall beside Beijing Railway Station. A fun place to watch different trains pass.

name: Chongwenmen
note: My usual base. Lots of Heytea; Taohua Yin Alley and Cuihualao are my tasty nearby picks.

name: National Art Museum of China
note: On my list, but I haven’t visited yet. Elsewhere in the eastern hutongs: Keneng Youshu for bookstore/cafe co-working, and Shifter for a bar.

name: Jingshan Park
note: Climb the hill for a spectacular city view. The field notes connect its construction to the Forbidden Palace moats and recall the last Ming emperor.

name: Beihai Park
note: A beautiful lake park with the White Dagoba. My memorable moment: a security guard watching videos at maximum volume.

name: Shichahai · Qianhai & Houhai
note: Crowded lakeside bars and live music, often streamed online. Kaorouji’s thinly sliced lamb with onions and spices is one of my favorite dishes. Also: Yinsan Douzhi.

name: Prince Kung’s Mansion
note: A luxurious traditional Chinese residence beyond the Palace.

name: Nanluoguxiang
note: A very touristy hutong. My food highlight is No. 69 Fangzhuanchang Noodles for zhajiangmian. Modernista is another bar recommendation in this part of town.

name: Drum Tower
note: Climb for the view, and photograph the red walls. Paired with the nearby Bell Tower in the field notes.

name: Bell Tower
note: The companion to the Drum Tower, with stairs and views over the surrounding hutongs.

name: Lama Temple
note: A working Tibetan Buddhist temple with spectacular art and statues. Kaorouwan is my nearby lamb recommendation.

name: Confucius Temple
note: Imagine studying for the imperial examinations. The field notes highlight the stone inscriptions of successful candidates.

name: Wudaoying Hutong
note: Little shops and a rooftop skyline view at Fuding Coffee.

name: Temple of Earth
note: A park with a central altar. Nearby Jindingxuan for Cantonese food.

name: Miaoying Temple
note: A Yuan-era pagoda. For a photograph, look down the alley by % Arabica. The field notes also mention a cat cafe and bookstore.

name: Temple of Ancient Monarchs
note: Where emperors paid tribute to rulers of previous dynasties.

name: Guangji Temple
note: A Buddhist temple and headquarters of the Buddhist Association of China.

name: Zhongnanhai
note: The central government and party compound. The field notes describe passing along Chang’an Street, rather than entering.

name: Sanlitun
note: Upscale shopping, Gentle Monster, and food. d.lounge is my nearby bar pick.

name: Workers’ Stadium
note: A nightlife cluster. The field notes describe table-based clubbing; PH is my music favorite. Dada is another recommendation for techno.

name: Chaoyang Park
note: A big park and the Labubu theme park. In the wider area: Slowboat for burgers and beer, and Oasis Lounge overlooking the Liangma River.

name: China World Trade Center
note: Luxury shopping and Rock & Ride, where I found a few pieces.

name: CCTV Headquarters
note: An architectural highlight near the World Trade Center.

name: Chaoyang Joy City
note: An enormous ten-story mall. The Tree is one of my aesthetic picks here.

name: Wangjing SOHO
note: An interesting architectural achievement.

name: 798 Art Zone
note: A former factory complex now home to contemporary artists and galleries. UCCA Center for Contemporary Art is an anchor.

name: Summer Palace
note: A sprawling palace landscape. My highlights are Wanshoushan and the Long Corridor, with plenty more to wander through.

name: Old Summer Palace
note: Palace ruins; my main highlight is Haiyantang and its Western-style ruins and zodiac fountain.

name: Peking University
note: The field notes suggest arranging an invitation from an affiliate before visiting. Check current campus access rules.

name: Tsinghua University
note: Another campus visit to arrange with an affiliate. My wider Haidian recommendations include AGI Bar, Catail Backyard, Laohuihui, Long Time Ago, Bistro Na, and Mizhong Shan; branches are not pinned.

name: Great Wall · Mutianyu
note: My quieter Great Wall option, with a longer journey to reach it.

name: Great Wall · Badaling
note: My Great Wall option for an easy high-speed rail trip, with bigger crowds.
